key_insight: For nonlinear PDEs, a first-order system least-squares residual can reliably measure solution error in the PDE-compliant norm under stability and smoothness conditions near a solution branch.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed neural operators with equation-aligned training losses and inference-time error indicators, without requiring labeled solutions for residual training.
method: Establish residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Verify conditions for monotone reaction, nonlinear diffusion, and compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity.
Train a reduced-basis neural operator in a conforming finite element space, using snapshots for the basis and finite element assembly for the loss and gradient.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that the square root of loss excess tracks error within factors comparable to the linear case, while the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm when evaluated in the same finite element space.
watch_item: Residual–error guarantees depend on the PDE and admissible region; some require proximity to a solution branch and regularity measured in a stronger norm.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
